maps.title: Who won each state, and by how much?
maps.caption: The winner's lead over the runner-up in every presidential election. Republican leads rise above the zero line and Democratic leads fall below it. Mississippi went from Roosevelt by 94 points in 1936 to Goldwater by 74 in 1964. Vermont went from Roosevelt (R) by 59 in 1904 to Harris by 31 in 2024.
maps.note: Light-blue bands on the zero line are third-party wins: Roosevelt's Bull Moose in 1912, La Follette in 1924, Thurmond in 1948 and Wallace in 1968. Leads over 60 points reach the tile edge. Alabama 1960 counts the Democratic slate of Kennedy and unpledged electors once.

maps.title: How does each state make electricity?
maps.caption: Share of net generation by fuel. Coal supplied 86% of Iowa's power in 1990 and 21% in 2024, while clean sources rose from 13% to 66%. West Virginia still makes 85% of its power from coal. Delaware swapped coal for gas.
maps.note: Clean is nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, geothermal and biomass. Pumped storage and "other" are excluded.
sources: EIA, net generation by state by energy source

maps.title: Who uses each state's energy?
maps.caption: Share of total energy consumed by sector. Industry uses 70% of Louisiana's energy and 56% of Texas's. Transportation takes 59% in Hawaii. In DC, industry fell from 28% in 1960 to 3%.
maps.note: Homes & businesses = residential + commercial. Energy measured in Btu.

maps.title: How does each state collect its taxes?
maps.caption: State government tax revenue by type. Light blue appears when a state adopts an income tax: Nebraska and Illinois had none in 1960 and over 40% of revenue from it by 2025. Texas and Nevada still have none. Most of Alaska's orange is oil severance tax.
maps.note: State taxes only; local taxes, including most property tax, are excluded. Biennial until 1950. DC has no state government.
sources: Census Bureau, Annual Survey of State Tax Collections

maps.title: How does each state earn a living?
maps.caption: Earnings by industry. Farming was 42% of North Dakota's earnings in 1929 and 6% in 2025. Manufacturing was 48% of Michigan's earnings in 1950 and is 15% now.
maps.note: Industry definitions change from SIC to NAICS in 2001. Negative farm earnings are set to zero.

maps.title: Who signs the paychecks?
maps.caption: Earnings by employer. World War II shows in nearly every tile: federal pay was 45% of Virginia's earnings in 1944 and 56% of DC's. In 1960 the federal government paid 43% of Alaska's earnings.
maps.note: Federal = federal civilian + military. A few suppressed values are interpolated.

maps.title: Where does the money come from?
maps.caption: Personal income by source. Government benefits were 2% of income in most states in 1929. They are 31% in West Virginia and 28% in Mississippi today. Florida gets 32% of its income from dividends, interest and rent.
maps.note: Work = net earnings by place of residence. Benefits = personal current transfer receipts (Social Security, Medicare, Medicaid and others).
sources: BEA, SAINC4 personal income by major component
